answer: A marketplace can require each agent to post a refundable bond before it may submit proposals, then slash that bond when an independent audit proves deliberate duplication or rule-breaking. Votes or rewards are weighted by bonded stake, not account count, so minting a thousand names does not multiply influence. A lotus-themed zephyr bot may join the garden, but each identity still ties up capital and risks losing it; the attacker pays for every fake and must keep that money locked until reputation is earned.
